runs.subject: N
runs.what: SQLite's give-back of free pages on Windows with the new store's settings (WAL, incremental auto-vacuum, mmap_size 4 GB; incremental_vacuum then wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)), Node's SQLite 3.53.4: half the rows of a 256.9 MB file deleted, then the give-back, with no other connection, with another process or a second connection holding the file mapped or unmapped. File size after the give-back (MB): alone 128.8; other process mapped 256.9 (still 256.9 after it closed and the give-back ran again); other process unmapped 128.8; second connection mapped 256.9 (also after it closed); second connection unmapped 128.8. Every give-back reported success. The mapping process's working set after reading the file: 309 MB with the map, 54 MB without
runs.command: node win-tools/store/sqlite-map-probe.mjs <dir> <out.json> 256 (Node 24.21.0, node:sqlite)

runs.subject: The new version and P
runs.what: the bar's rerail-native corpus (git archive 53f5b92a1 -- native/src from a checkout of the new version and of 0.1.5, extracted with Windows' tar, hashed as the bar hashes it), with Git LFS files and with GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1, each with core.autocrlf false and true. With LFS files: 385 files, df111caf..., the pin, under both line-end settings. Skipped: 385 files, bb80e5e4..., under both. No file of the corpus holds a CR byte but the binary names.bin: line ends play no part, since .gitattributes says * text=auto eol=lf and git archive reads the archived tree's attributes
runs.command: git worktree add <sha> (with and without GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1); git -c core.autocrlf=<false|true> archive -o x.tar 53f5b92a1 -- native/src; tar -xf x.tar; node hash-tree.mjs (the bar's hashTree). Order of values: N skip false, N skip true, N lfs false, N lfs true, then the same for 0.1.5

runs.subject: The new version and P
runs.what: the file the .rr side's engine program build reads first among its LFS files, native/grammars/tree-sitter-sql/src/parser.generated.c.gz, in a checkout of the new version and of 0.1.5: with Git LFS files it is the 1,626,241-byte gzip file; with GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1 it is a 132-byte pointer starting 'version https://git-lfs', the test of native/src/build_grammars.rs:270 that panics 'is a Git LFS pointer, not the file' in the build script of rerail-lang (as in the measuring machine's build log). The same at both commits: not new in the new version
runs.command: git worktree add <sha> with and without GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1; size and first bytes of the file. Order: N skip, N lfs, 0.1.5 skip, 0.1.5 lfs. The cargo build itself was not repeated on Windows: neither check machine has a Rust toolchain; the measuring machine's log of the failed run shows the panic

findings.title: The test the description names no longer waits 10 s
findings.what: The description says the audit-cli scan test waits 10 s for a scan that takes 11.8 s on Windows, left so the test keeps showing the slowdown. At aad1dd6ef the test (test/cli/audit-cli.test.ts:271) waits for the scan through the daemon API for up to 60 s (#711, merged into both 0.1.5 and the branch), so it passes either way and no longer shows the slowdown; the scan's own duration still does, and is measured here.
evidence: code: test/cli/audit-cli.test.ts:271-301 at aad1dd6ef and at 9cad73564, commit 919e55d87
findings.severity: low: the description is out of date

findings.title: The new version ends five rule runs at their work budget that 0.1.5 finishes, and reports six findings fewer
findings.what: On this repository's own TypeScript (602 files) the typescript pack gives 12,578 findings at the new version against 12,584 at 0.1.5, the same in each of the new version's three runs. N reports 5 budget-exceeded failures (a rule stopped on a file when it spent its allowance of work) that 0.1.5 does not, and one more source-incomplete. A person sees fewer findings and, in rerail status or the audit, files a rule could not finish. The budget is a count of work, not of time, so it is not the Windows machine's speed.
evidence: code: the budget-exceeded failures are counts of work (native/src/code_rule_dsl/workspace/evaluate.rs:757 match budget, :997 visited nodes against limits.visits_for, at aad1dd6ef)
findings.severity: medium: findings lost on real code; the bar does not gate findings on real code

findings.title: The shippability bar needs the pack data even for its real-code corpora
findings.what: prepare builds every pack's fixtures corpus first and stops at the first missing recording ("... fixtures.expected.json is missing: run node scripts/s3/pack-fixtures.mjs pull"), and exporting a git ref as the baseline pulls the pack data too, so without access to the project's pack data storage nothing is measured, on any system. A three-line local change (patches/shipbar-no-pack-data.patch) marks such a fixtures corpus absent and lets the six packs whose real-code corpus is a commit of the repository run; the baseline is given as a checkout folder.
evidence: bsw-bar-chk2 out.log: shipbar: fixtures rust: {"absent":"the pack test data is not pulled ..."} with the patch
findings.severity: low: contributors outside the project cannot run the bar

findings.title: A checkout without Git LFS files makes the bar stop before it measures, with a message that does not say why
findings.what: The rust pack's real-code corpus (native/src at 53f5b92a1) holds names.bin, a Git LFS file. Without LFS files git archive writes the 131-byte pointer, the corpus hashes to bb80e5e4... instead of the pinned df111caf..., and the bar exits 2 ("corpus rerail-native is 385 files, ...; corpora.json pins 385 files, ...") before any run. With LFS files the corpus matches on Windows. Smallest fix: in buildReal (scripts/ship/shipbar.ts:351-355 at aad1dd6ef), after extracting a git corpus, refuse any file that starts with 'version https://git-lfs' and name it, with the remedy the engine build already gives (native/src/build_grammars.rs:270, LFS_POINTER at :288): '<corpus>: <path> is a Git LFS pointer, not the file: run git lfs install && git lfs pull'. Steps: GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1 (or a clone made without git-lfs), then npm run bench:ship -- prepare --baseline <dir> --out <dir> --packs rust. Not specific to Windows.
findings.severity: low: a confusing stop; build:native already names LFS in its own check

findings.title: On Windows the store gives no disk back while another connection has it mapped, and says nothing
findings.what: With the new store's settings (WAL, incremental auto-vacuum, a memory map; its give-back: incremental_vacuum, then wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)), half the rows of a 256.9 MB file deleted: alone, the give-back shrinks the file to 128.8 MB; with another process holding the file mapped, SQLite reports success (no error, nothing busy) and the file stays 256.9 MB, and it still is after that process closed and the give-back ran again. A person sees no error; the store file keeps its largest size on disk until a later write and checkpoint run with no map open. The new store opens every connection with the map on (native/src/content_store/connection.rs:444-447, 4 GB unless RERAIL_STORE_MMAP_MB says otherwise), so its own upkeep gives pages back beside mapped connections whenever another of them is open. 0.1.5 opens its store with the map off.
evidence: code: native/src/content_store/connection.rs:444-447 and upkeep.rs:190-210 at aad1dd6ef; 0.1.5 sets mmap_size 0 (connection.rs:321 at 9cad73564)
findings.severity: medium: disk use only; no error and no lost result

not_measured.what: the shippability bar on the fixtures corpora of every pack, and on the sample corpora of blade, next, php, python, react, sql and vue
not_measured.why: both come from the pack data archives, which need read access to the project's pack data storage; no machine of ours has it (an unsigned request is refused, 403)
not_measured.would_take: the same Windows run with the pack data pulled: npm run fixtures:pull on a machine signed in to the storage, then npm run bench:ship -- run --corpus all

not_measured.what: the bar's user waits (W1 to W8: hooks, CLI and daemon through each build) on Windows
not_measured.why: shipbar.ts refuses them off Linux by design: "waits measure on Linux only (taskset, the page cache drop)" (scripts/ship/shipbar.ts, main())
not_measured.would_take: a Windows way to pin and to empty the file cache in waits.ts; the hook and CLI waits on Windows will be measured with the hook-cost harness instead

not_measured.what: the shippability bar on Windows, the new version against 0.1.5: wall time cold and warm, CPU, peak memory and findings on the six packs whose real-code corpus is a commit of the repository, both of the new version's ways to run rules (its packs through the product path, and the .rr rewrites on the new engine)
not_measured.why: it needs the measuring machine alone, which only a start from the workstation that schedules our measuring machines can claim; the run started at 18:04 UTC and its results come in a later commit
not_measured.would_take: one alone run of about one to two hours on the Windows measuring machine

not_measured.what: the product under a 20-minute load with about 190 worktrees on Windows, the new version, 0.1.5 and main + six fixes: the daemon's CPU, heap growth, working set and committed memory at the peak, hook p95 against its floor, failed hooks, probes answered
not_measured.why: a load run needs the measuring machine alone, started from the workstation that schedules our measuring machines
not_measured.would_take: four alone runs of about 25 minutes each (the new version, 0.1.5, main + six fixes, the new version again)

not_measured.what: a hook's cost per daemon state on the slowed Windows machine for the new version, 0.1.5 and main + six fixes, processes per hook for 0.1.5 and main + six fixes, the upgrade wait measured alone, and a fresh daemon's first event in a repository of 153 worktrees
not_measured.why: the slowed machine saturates its CPUs, a run only the workstation that schedules our measuring machines can start; the harness was checked at the new version here, not alone
not_measured.would_take: one alone run of several hours on the second Windows machine

not_measured.what: the Windows unit test set's time at the new version against 0.1.5, for the CI shards' 60 and 90 minute limits
not_measured.why: a whole unit set holds a Windows machine for about an hour per build; the check machines were full all afternoon, and our machines are not the CI runner
not_measured.would_take: the unit set at the new version and at 0.1.5 alone on the measuring machine; vitest.log gives each file's time

not_measured.what: the audit-cli repository scan's time at the new version against 0.1.5 on Windows (the description's 11.8 s against 10.0 s)
not_measured.why: both Windows test machines were full all afternoon: a five-round repeat waited in line on each and never started (one was cancelled while it waited, the other gave up its caller after 90 minutes)
not_measured.would_take: five rounds of the new version and 0.1.5 in turn, alone, about 20 minutes

not_measured.what: the store's give-back beside the new version's own daemon (a scan through a session fills the store, then half its pages freed and given back while the daemon runs, with the map on and off), and the upgrade from 0.1.5 to the new version beside a plain restart of 0.1.5
not_measured.why: the only Windows machine free for it, a workstation on a hard disk shared with about 20 test runs, took over 40 minutes per dependency install; the run was stopped at this part's time limit
not_measured.would_take: the hook-cost harness's ST and UP phases on a machine with a fast disk; the slowed-machine run already holds UP:P:N and UP:P:P

notes.text: When the measuring started (15:50 UTC on 17 November) the npm registry listed @neralabs/rerail up to 0.1.4; 0.1.5 was published at 15:57 UTC. 0.1.5 is built here from tag v0.1.5 (9cad73564) the same way as the new version (release engine from npm run build:native, npm ci); its release-form Linux engine (41.3 MB) matches the published package's to 0.2%.
